tasks.title: Repair idempotent inventory reservations
tasks.provenance: Locally authored synthetic task fixture with real model-driven tool interaction; not SWE-bench, internet research, or production customer data.
tasks.prompt:
Repair the stockflow reservation package. It has bugs across multiple files. Public cases are examples, not the full specification.
normalize_items(items) strips whitespace and lowercases SKU strings, sums quantities for duplicate normalized SKUs, accepts only positive non-bool integers, and rejects empty SKUs or invalid quantities with ValueError.
apply_event(stock, held, event) returns (new_available, new_held), never mutating any input, including nested items. Stock keys are already normalized. Reservation IDs strip surrounding whitespace but are case-sensitive. reserve normalizes the basket and checks all stock before allocating; insufficient or missing stock raises ValueError. Replaying an active reservation with an identical normalized basket is an idempotent no-op; the same ID with a different basket raises ValueError. release restores quantities by addition, removes the reservation, and is a no-op if the ID is unknown. Unknown event kind or empty ID raises ValueError. An ID may be reserved again after release. replay applies events in order and returns {available, held}.
Read files, edit only the three stockflow Python files and run immutable public cases if useful. Finish with a concise natural-language explanation. The objective grade runs additional hidden cases after you finish, not through tools.

tasks.title: Repair invoice rounding and idempotent refunds
tasks.provenance: Locally authored synthetic task fixture with real model-driven tool interaction; not SWE-bench, internet research, or production customer data.
tasks.prompt:
Repair the billing package using integer arithmetic only. discounted_line(unit_cents, quantity, discount_bps) calculates unit_cents * quantity * (10000 - discount_bps) / 10000 rounded to nearest integer cents, with exact halves rounded upward. Round each invoice line independently before summing. Inputs must be non-bool integers; unit_cents >= 0, quantity > 0, and 0 <= discount_bps <= 10000; otherwise raise ValueError. Empty invoice total is zero.
settle(lines, refunds) returns gross_cents, refunded_cents, net_cents. Refund ID strings strip outer whitespace, stay case-sensitive, and cannot be empty. amount_cents is a nonnegative non-bool integer. Repeated refund ID with equal amount is idempotent; the same ID with different amount raises ValueError. Total unique refunds exceeding the invoice raises ValueError. Net is gross minus refunded. No function may mutate any input, including nested dictionaries. Bugs span the money and adjustment logic; public cases are incomplete examples.
Edit only the three billing Python files. Public cases are immutable. Finish with a concise natural-language explanation; additional hidden cases are scored only after final completion.
